thesis_summary.thesis: Bursa Malaysia Berhad operates Malaysia's national stock exchange and related marketplace infrastructure. **[Fact]** Customers pay trading and clearing fees on cash equities and derivatives, listing and depository charges, Islamic market (Bursa Suq Al-Sila') fees, and market-data subscriptions. **[Fact]** FY2024 operating revenue was **RM757.7 million** (+27.8% versus last year) and profit attributable to owners was **RM310.1 million** (`official-reports/2024-12-31_Condensed_Report_Q4.pdf`). **[Fact]** The group had **809.3 million** ordinary shares outstanding and net assets per share of **RM1.08** at 31 December 2024 (same filing). **[Fact]** Q1 2025 operating revenue was **RM177.7 million** (-1.7% year-over-year) with owners' profit **RM68.4 million** (-8.8%) (`official-reports/2025-03-31_Condensed_Report_Q1.pdf`). The exchange also runs Bursa Carbon Exchange and digital investor channels under the refreshed multi-asset exchange brand.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: There is no dated structural discount or catalyst stack here. **[Inference]** FY2024 was a strong volume year (operating revenue +27.8%, IPO count 20 versus 7 in 2023) and the stock trades near **27×** trailing earnings on KLSE screens; the market may treat peak trading activity as a new normal. **[Inference]** Our base return uses mid-cycle owner cash below FY2024 spot free cash flow and below the **40 sen** total dividend declared for FY2024. **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **cycle normalization** on Malaysia average daily value (ADV), not an equity yield curve or K-1 exclusion story.
